blocks.caption: Biological functions of proteins
rows: control or regulate growth, development, metabolism and reproduction
insulin, made by the pancreas, regulates the movement of glucose from the blood into cells
store nutrients for growing seedlings or the early development of animals
ferritin stores iron (in some bacteria and in plant and animal tissues)
the most abundant proteins in vertebrates; fibrous; give shape and support
keratin in hair, fibrin in blood clots, collagen in skin, ligaments, tendons and bones
make up the thin and thick filaments of muscle; contraction and relaxation
antibodies bind specific antigens (proteins on pathogens) and destroy them
move molecules and ions round the body and across membranes
haemoglobin: oxygen binds to its iron as blood travels between the lungs and the tissues
in cell membranes; receive chemical signals and pass on responses

blocks.prompt: Keratin in hair, nails, horns and feathers is strong, flexible and not easily denatured. Is this due mainly to hydrogen bonds or disulphide bonds?
blocks.explanation: Disulphide bonds: they are covalent S-S cross-links between chains, much stronger than hydrogen bonds, so heat and mild chemicals do not easily break them.

blocks.prompt: How can two peptides with the same kinds and numbers of amino acids differ in primary structure?
blocks.explanation: The amino acids can be joined in a different order (sequence).

blocks.prompt: What are the two most common secondary structures in our body?
blocks.explanation: The alpha-helix and the beta-pleated sheet.

blocks.prompt: Why does a denatured protein no longer work properly?
blocks.explanation: Denaturation breaks the bonds that hold its secondary and tertiary structure, so the protein loses its specific 3D shape (for an enzyme, the shape of its active site), and its function depends on that shape.

blocks.prompt: Why does egg white solidify on heating?
blocks.explanation: Heat breaks the hydrogen bonds holding the globular albumin chains folded; the chains unfold, tangle and bond to each other, forming an insoluble solid (denaturation).

items: Proteins act as hormones (insulin), stores (ferritin), structure (keratin, collagen), muscle (actin, myosin), defence (antibodies), transport (haemoglobin), receptors and regulators.
